subject: Privilege guardrails discovery + retention qualifiers
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>

Subject: Privilege guardrails discovery + retention qualifiers

Hi Lisa — great conversation this morning, thanks for taking the time. Quick recap from our side and a short ask list so we can scope next steps:

Recap (what we heard)
- You ingest customer PII fields (full name, email, payment token last4) for transactional features and some enrichment flows.
- Two retention windows: short-term raw logs (90 days) and longer-term billing/records (7 years) driven by compliance.
- EU customers require EU residency for primary data; global contracts may allow cross-border logging for metrics only.
- Support access is tightly controlled today — break-glass requires VP approval and is audited.

Open questions / asks
1) Can you confirm the legal/regulatory citation that mandates the 7-year billing retention? (this affects our proposed retention tiers)
2) For EU residency, is it required for all data or only for directly identifiable customer records?
3) Would you be able to share a short list of support roles that need read access vs write/admin access for our RBAC mapping?
4) Are you comfortable with a customer-managed KMS for encryption-at-rest, or do you need Redwood-managed keys?

Proposed next steps
- 30–45m technical walkthrough with Aditya + Monica to validate RBAC options and retention knobs. Proposed slot: Wed Apr 22 9:00am PT.
- Share any existing security artifacts (SOC2, retention policy) so our Security/Privacy teams can confirm fit.
- We'll prepare an initial RBAC matrix and two retention configuration options (90d/7y vs tiered erasable logs) prior to the call.

Attachments: redwood-security-overview.pdf (pdf)

Thanks — I’ll coordinate calendar invites once I hear back on availability and the artifact list.

Sean Gallagher

Thanks Sean — appreciate the clear recap. Answers inline and attachments attached.

On Apr 18, 2026, at 9:12 AM, Sean Gallagher wrote:
> Hi Lisa — great conversation this morning, thanks for taking the time. Quick recap from our side and a short ask list so we can scope next steps:

Answers / clarifications:
- PII: correct — we store name, email, payment token last4, plus a hashed customer id used for analytics.
- Retention: billing and audit records must be kept 7 years per our internal compliance policy tied to tax/regulatory audits (US Internal Revenue Code/our legal counsel). Raw request logs are kept 90 days and then rotated to an aggregated metrics store.
- Residency: for EU customers we keep primary customer records in the EU tenant; aggregated telemetry can be replicated out of region for performance/monitoring.
- Support access: break-glass is VP approval + 2FA step-up, all actions are logged to our SIEM and immutable storage for 7 years.
- KMS: We prefer customer-managed KMS for production keys; however for pilot projects we can consider vendor-managed keys with strict MFA and audit.

Attachments: FinServ-Security-Controls-answers.docx (docx, 120KB)

We can do Apr 22 9:00am PT. Please include your SE and an architecture checklist so we can confirm gaps during the call.

Lisa Wong
Head of Security Programs | FinServ Corp
lisa.wong@finserv.com

Internal notes — forwarding next actions based on Lisa’s answers. Not for external distribution.

Key takeaways:
- 7-year retention is non-negotiable for billing/audit records; need legal citation or confirmation from their counsel to finalize retention SLAs.
- EU residency requirement applies to primary customer records only; telemetry may be global. Good — this maps to our tenant/region routing options.

Ask for Aditya (priority)
- Draft RBAC mapping (roles -> read vs write vs admin) for: Support Agent, Support Manager, Security Analyst, Engineering On-call. Include justification for least-privilege defaults.
- Provide two implementation options for break-glass: (A) time-limited vaulted access with VP approval + audit trail; (B) emergency support token with post-hoc approval and automated rotation. Outline pros/cons for compliance and ops.
- Sample retention configs: option 1 (raw logs 90d, billed records 7y immutable), option 2 (90d + 12mo warm archive + 7y cold immutable). Include expected storage delta and ingestion impact.

I’ll draft the sec/contract language to propose for the DPA. Sean — after Aditya posts the matrix, I’ll include it in the invite for the Wed call.

Monica Patel

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Apr 2026 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Privilege guardrails discovery + retention qualifiers

Adding initial artifacts — see attached stubs. High-level notes below; I’ll walk through on Wed.

Attachments: rbac-matrix-sample.csv, retention-options.md

Technical summary (short):
- RBAC: propose role set and minimum privileges:
  * Support Agent: view-customer-data (redacted), open-tickets, annotate. No export/download.
  * Support Manager: same + escalate, request break-glass (approval flow).
  * Security Analyst: read access to full logs (privileged view) but requires just-in-time approval for live PII.
  * SRE/Engineering On-call: no PII access by default; elevated sessions for debug with time-limited credentials and logging.

- Break-glass options:
  A) Vaulted short-lived credentials issued after VP approval, recorded to immutable audit store. Best for auditability.
  B) Emergency token pre-provisioned with mandatory post-incident review and auto-rotation. Faster but higher risk; acceptable only with compensating controls.

- Logging & retention knobs:
  * Operational logs: 90 days live, then deduped/aggregated to 12 months warm archive.
  * Billing/audit records: immutable cold store 7 years (WORM) with legal custody markers.
  * Audit exports to customer SIEM via signed syslog over TLS; we recommend checksum + object versioning for immutability.

I’ll attach the CSV and short MD with storage estimates before the call.

— Aditya
